notes: lane/idxclient: the chat takes typed input. Java side, oracle/harness/netherite/oracle/ChatInput.java: a tick's keyboard and mouse events (one ["chat", mods, px, py, clip, comp, events] tape op) go into LWJGL's read buffers and vanilla GuiScreen.handleInput runs them once over the screen that is up (the modifiers and the pointer are the poll's one state for the batch; a key that closes the screen leaves the rest to the closed GuiChat, as vanilla's loop does: Enter, Enter sends twice). Native, gui_chat.c: GuiChat, GuiSleepMP and GuiTextField over UTF-16 text, the sent history, the clipboard (the op carries it for a paste), tab completion (C14, the S3A back through gui_chat_tab_reply); the C01 goes to chatcmd.c (processChatMessage, chat.type.text, the spam counter, the commands a player without cheats reaches). The live client maps T and slash, SDL's text and keys into the batch (play.c chat_event, chat_batch). idx-chattype-s1 (every editing key with the modifiers, the clipboard, the history, the double Enter, Escape, tab completion of commands, arguments and names, every command path, a click on a name and a shift-click) and idx-chatsleep-s1 (typing and tab completion in bed, Escape and Leave Bed) replay every row in test_snapshots and play_check with 0 mismatches; idx-chatdraw-s1 and idx-chathover-s1 draw within 4 to 16 px. The chat spam kick (disconnect.spam, eleven messages inside about a second) stops the native session as not modelled; a history over GC_HIST (64) entries deep likewise.
